supporting_observations.claim: At 13:40 UTC, ana.ruiz ran PowerShell to compress \\FILE-PIN-01\Shared\Clients into C:\Users\ana.ruiz\AppData\Local\Temp\c.zip; the archive was created shortly afterward.
At 13:45:50 UTC, the proxy recorded a 51,000,000-byte client-to-server transfer from WS-ARUIZ-01 to dropzone-transfer.net:443 under ana.ruiz’s identity.
The transfer was made by Chrome on WS-ARUIZ-01, corroborated by the endpoint network events for the same proxy connection.

The close sequence of compressing client-share data and sending a large outbound transfer to an unapproved file-transfer destination strongly supports suspected data exfiltration as the alerted activity.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records show the destination and transfer volume but do not expose the contents of the TLS tunnel or identify the uploaded object. (T079-00174, T079-00176)
The available records do not directly correlate c.zip with the outbound transfer or provide the archive’s size. (T079-00143, T079-00145, T079-00174, T079-00176)
The proxy status and byte counts do not establish whether the remote service accepted or retained the transferred data. (T079-00174, T079-00176)
claims_not_established: That c.zip, or any particular file from the Clients share, was the payload of the transfer.
The contents or sensitivity of the transferred data.
Who controlled dropzone-transfer.net or whether the transfer had any specific external recipient.
Whether the transfer completed successfully at the application level or whether an authorization existed outside the provided inventory.
additional_evidence_needed: Proxy or TLS-inspection records identifying the HTTP request, upload object or filename, and application-level result for the dropzone-transfer.net session.
Endpoint file-access and archive metadata, including the size and contents or hash of c.zip and access to the source files under \\FILE-PIN-01\Shared\Clients.
User and business-owner confirmation of whether the transfer was authorized, plus available endpoint and proxy evidence tying the browser upload to the staged archive.
unrelated_findings: After the alerted transfer, ana.ruiz’s Chrome session browsed Google Drive, an unapproved file-sharing service in the provided inventory. Treat this as a separate finding; these records do not show that data was uploaded there. (T079-00197, T079-00198, T079-00213, T079-00219)

A SYSTEM PowerShell process ran C:\Scripts\service-health.ps1 and explicitly used svc-billing credentials from WS-ARUIZ-01. This is outside the alerted transfer; the change calendar notes a svc-billing rotation at 13:30, but the supplied records do not establish the script’s purpose or legitimacy. (T079-00178, T079-00180)
A taskhostw.exe process on WS-ARUIZ-01 explicitly used svc-bkp credentials. This is separate from the alerted transfer and warrants independent review. (T079-00414)
